text.p: - Only one out of four ministerial candidates proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek on Friday passed a parliamentary board hearing on Tueasday. In spite of the negative result Drnovsek does not have to withdraw any of his candidates.

- Number of crimes in Slovenia in 1996 fell by four percent compared to the previous year, while the number of traffic accidents decreased by six percent in the same period, the ministry for internal affairs said.
- Representatives of employers and trade unions will start coordinating their proposals on Wednesday in order to draw up a new agreement determining workers benefits.
- Slovenia's industrial output in December rose 7.9 percent compared to the same month in 1995, the statistical office reported.
- In 1996 the number of foreign over-night stays in Slovenia fell to 5.83 million, a one percent decrease from 1995, the statistical office said.
- Teenage ski-jumper Primoz Peterka, overall World Cup leader, was nominated as Slovenia's sportsman of the year in a survey conducted by daily Dnevnik.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan met Albanian ambassador Napoleon Roshi on Tuesday after he finished his four year term in Slovenia.
- November's foreign exchange reserves rose 27 percent to $4.3 billion, the Bank of Slovenia said.
- Shares of bank SKB jumped 20 percent on Tuesday after it returned to trading after its one-week suspension.
- Foreign investors are interested in investing in banks, as well as in Slovenian food processing and drug companies, an analyst at Bank Austria said.
